citation: Dahlstrom, Daniel O. 2019. "Missing in Action: Affectivity in Being and Time." In Heidegger on Affect, edited by Christos Hadjioannou, 105–126. Philosophers in Depth. Cham: Palgrave Macmillan. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-24639-6_5
discipline: philosophy (Heideggerian phenomenology; internal critique of Being and Time)
thesis: Heidegger 'talks the talk' about the equiprimordial, foundational status of affectivity (disposedness/Befindlichkeit, mood/Stimmung, feeling, emotion) in Being and Time but does not consistently 'walk the walk': across concern, tool-use, spatiality, being-with, das Man, and -- most consequentially -- the account of authentic conscience and anticipatory resoluteness, affectivity is repeatedly asserted as equiprimordial with understanding yet left lexically subordinated, omitted, or named without elaboration. The chapter is a BT-internal consistency audit, not an engagement with Heidegger's boredom analysis (FCM); 'boredom' occurs exactly once in the entire chapter, inside a citation of a companion essay's title.

sections.title: The Essentialness of Affectivity -- sympathetic reconstruction of disposedness's three essential characters (thrownness; equiprimordial disclosure of world/others/existence; world-openness/mattering); existential/existentiel distinction; structural analyses of fear and angst with their temporal characters

Gleichursprünglichkeit (Equiprimordiality) -- the lexical asymmetry befindliches Verstehen (14x) vs. verstehende Befindlichkeit (4x); Seinsverständnis ubiquitous, no parallel Seinsbefindlichkeit/Seinsstimmung

Begleitphänomenen (Accompanying Phenomena) -- survey of BT passages (concern, tool-use, significance, spatiality, Mitsein, das Man, idle talk, ambiguity, curiosity, fallenness) for presence/absence of affective analysis

Angst-Bereit (Angst-Preparedness) -- authentic conscience, guilt, angst-preparedness, anticipatory resoluteness, 'sober angst' and 'armed joy' (SZ 296-310); critique of the 'basic moods exceed fundamental ontology' scope-disclaimer as a dodge
Concluding Remark -- restates thesis; closes on the unresolved question of fundamental ontology's own corresponding mood

Endnotes 1-29, including the defense of 'disposedness' as translation (n.1, cross-referencing Elpidorou and Freeman 2015a) and the deferral of BT's temporal architecture to Elpidorou and Freeman (2015b) (n.16)

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: treated substantively as the object of angst (not boredom): angst discloses the meaninglessness of innerworldly beings and of Dasein's own being-in-the-world as such

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: oblique -- curiosity's restless distractedness and fallenness's sedating tranquility of absorption (Wirbel/whirlwind metaphor) as inauthentic, affectively-marked modes of worldly engagement

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: not treated for boredom specifically; the general fear/angst temporal architecture (Gewesenheit, awaiting vs. anticipatory running-ahead) that underlies any such analysis is treated at length; boredom's own temporal treatment explicitly deferred to the companion essay (bor-sec-03)
constructs.locus: p.109-111; n.16 p.123 (P/anticipatory-application for the boredom link)

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: not named as such, but structurally anticipated: moods and their underlying disposedness can be 'transparent'/occluded from the Dasein having them

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: not treated; 'boredom' appears exactly once in the chapter, only inside a citation of Elpidorou and Freeman (2015b)'s title

readings.text: Disposedness has three essential characters (SZ §29, GA 20): (1) thrownness-disclosure, the passivity of moods (Greek pathe/pathos vs. praxis); (2) 'an existentially basic sort' of the equiprimordial disclosedness of world, others, and existence; (3) Dasein's openness to the world and its mattering.

Disposedness (existential/ontological) is not identical with mood/feeling/emotion (existentiel/ontic); a mood is 'an exponent of disposedness' (GA 20:353); in an Aristotelian idiom, moods are 'first for us' while disposedness is 'first by nature.'

Moods and the disposedness underlying them are frequently occluded from the subject who has them; we 'can be oblivious to the disposedness underlying and co-constituting the mood,' which is why the existential phenomenologist must make explicit what moods do not themselves display.

Fear and angst receive masterful structural analyses with contrasting temporal characters: fear (awaiting a determinate worldly threat, inauthentic assimilation to the handy) vs. angst (no awaiting; resolute anticipation disclosing the meaninglessness of the world and of one's own being-in-the-world).

Central critical thesis: despite Heidegger's explicit doctrine that disposedness and understanding are equiprimordial (SZ 160, 220), his own prose privileges understanding -- 'disposed understanding' (befindliches Verstehen) occurs at least fourteen times vs. only four occurrences of the reverse order; 'Seinsverständnis' is ubiquitous with no comparable 'Seinsbefindlichkeit.'

A section-by-section survey (concern, tool-use, circumspection, significance, spatiality, being-with, solicitude) finds affectivity largely absent from analyses that, on Heidegger's own equiprimordiality thesis, should contain it -- most 'egregiously' from the account of being-with-others, where affect is 'conspicuously... absent.'

Curiosity and fallenness are the chapter's counter-examples: Heidegger is fully explicit about curiosity's restlessness/excitement and fallenness's sedating tranquility (the Wirbel/whirlwind metaphor for 'this dizzying plunge into nothingness'), showing he can attend to affect fully but does so inconsistently.

The authenticity case sharpens the stakes: Heidegger asks what mood corresponds to 'wanting-to-have-a-conscience' (the uncanniness of conscience, disclosed via the disposedness of angst) and later names 'sober angst' and 'armed joy' as the mood of anticipatory resoluteness, but these allusions are 'meager to a fault' given how much of the temporality/authenticity analysis rests on them.

Heidegger's scope-disclaimer -- that elaborating 'basic moods' like joy oversteps fundamental-ontological (vs. philosophical-anthropological) inquiry -- is judged 'a dodge or diversion,' since he freely enlists moods (curiosity, tranquility, uncanniness) elsewhere when it suits his purposes.
Concluding, unresolved aporia: the 'missing in action' pattern may be 'of a piece' with a further absence -- BT nowhere names the mood corresponding to doing fundamental ontology itself.

concepts.gloss: the basic existential of being disposed; discloses that and how Dasein is, prior to and independent of any subject/object split
the existentiel/ontic correlate felt through disposedness; irreducible to knowing or willing
the doctrine that disposedness and understanding are co-equal, non-derivative existentials
the demoted status (since Aristotle, per Heidegger's own diagnosis) of emotions/feelings as a third class of mental phenomena alongside presenting and willing
the ubiquitous BT expression for Dasein's understanding of being; has no affective parallel in Heidegger's usage
anxiety, analyzed structurally in parallel with fear; noted as named both a ground-disposedness and a ground-mood at SZ 188-190, 310
the anonymous 'they-self'; idle talk, ambiguity, and curiosity surveyed for affective content
falling into worldly absorption as flight from one's own thrownness; the 'sedating tranquility' and the Wirbel (whirlwind) metaphor
wanting-to-have-a-conscience, uncanniness, angst-preparedness, anticipatory resoluteness -- the chapter's central test case
philological aside: the root 'mut' in German 'zumute' is cognate with English 'mood' per the OED

interlocutors.name: Martin Heidegger
interlocutors.role: primary text under analysis (Being and Time; also GA 20, Prolegomena zur Geschichte des Zeitbegriffs)

interlocutors.name: Andreas Elpidorou and Lauren Freeman
interlocutors.role: cited twice by name: (2015a) for a fuller Befindlichkeit/Stimmung translation survey; (2015b) for the temporal dimensions of affectivity (and, in that companion essay, boredom) -- both explicitly deferred-to rather than re-argued here

interlocutors.name: Lauren Freeman (2016, solo)
interlocutors.role: cited early for the phrase 'attuned through mood' to open the chapter's positive reconstruction

interlocutors.name: Eugene Gendlin
interlocutors.role: cited (1978/1979) for the claim that Befindlichkeit is 'both inward and outward but prior to their differentiation,' supporting 'disposedness' as translation

interlocutors.name: Aristotle
interlocutors.role: source of the 'first for us' vs. 'first by nature' priority distinction applied to moods vs. disposedness; also cited (n.29) on hexis/pathos/hedone against Heidegger's 1924 lectures on the Grundbegriffe der aristotelischen Philosophie (GA 18)

interlocutors.name: Max Scheler
interlocutors.role: credited (with Kant, Mendelssohn, Hamilton) for continuing a tradition asserting affectivity's irreducibility to knowing/willing that Heidegger extends, while also faulting the tradition (including implicitly Scheler) for lacking ontological interpretation

interlocutors.name: Immanuel Kant
interlocutors.role: historical source (with Tetens, Mendelssohn, Hamilton, Brentano) of the tripartite classification of mental faculties (feeling/understanding/will) that Heidegger's 'accompanying phenomena' critique targets

interlocutors.name: Rene Descartes
interlocutors.role: cited as the (unsurprising) case where affectivity is absent -- the bloodless determination of the world as res extensa

tensions.label: Equiprimordiality-in-doctrine vs. equiprimordiality-in-practice
tensions.poles: Heidegger's explicit doctrine that disposedness and understanding are equiprimordial existentials (SZ 160, 220) vs. his own lexical/structural practice, which privileges understanding throughout (befindliches Verstehen 14x vs. verstehende Befindlichkeit 4x; Seinsverständnis ubiquitous, no Seinsbefindlichkeit)

tensions.label: Fundamental-ontology's scope-disclaimer vs. its own selective affective elaboration
tensions.poles: Heidegger's repeated claim that analyzing 'basic moods' like joy oversteps a properly ontological (vs. anthropological) inquiry (SZ 17, 49f., 131, 183, 194, 200, 301) vs. his freely enlisting moods (curiosity, tranquility, uncanniness) elsewhere when it suits his purposes

tensions.label: Anxiety vs. profound boredom as candidate Grundstimmung (continues bor-sec-02's DA3)
tensions.poles: bor-sec-02 flags that 'Grundstimmung' appears only once in BT (SZ 358/310) and becomes central only after 1929, in FCM; this chapter independently corroborates the same rarity, locating Angst named as both Grundbefindlichkeit and Grundstimmung at exactly SZ 310 -- inside the resoluteness passage this chapter's own §3 treats as its thinnest point of affective elaboration
